newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank head urges full convertibility.
newsitem.headline: China central bank head urges full convertibility.

text.p: China's central bank governor, Dai Xianglong, has urged government departments to study the feasibility of making China's yuan currency fully convertible as soon as possible.
"Though we have not worked out a timetable for the yuan's free convertibility, it should be regarded as a subject for earnest study," the Xinhua news agency on Tuesday quoted Dai as saying.

The full convertibility of the yuan was of great significance to strengthening ties between China and other countries, it quoted Dai, head of the People's Bank of China, as telling a meeting of heads of provincial branches of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE).
On December 1, China announced its yuan had become convertible on the current account.
A SAFE spokesman said it was China's long-term goal to make the yuan convertible on the capital account.
However, the government had no specific timetable for free convertibility, the spokesman said.
Currently, China exercises strict control on the capital account to avoid fluctuations on the financial market, Xinhua said.
Officials have said they would like to see the yuan convertible on the capital account by the end of the century.
